content.title: About
content.content: Dry rice cereal for toddlers is designed for children from 6 months old. It contains 100 % whole rice and is fortified with iron, vitamin C and folic acid. The cereal dissolves easily in warm water or milk, creating a soft, easily digestible meal without added sugar or salt.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Rice is one of the most hypoallergenic grains, making the cereal suitable for most children.
Dry cereal has a long shelf life and does not require refrigeration.
No artificial flavors, colors or preservatives are used.
The cereal can be prepared with breast milk, formula or water, allowing easy adaptation.
Each serving provides about 20 % of the daily iron requirement for children 6–12 months.

items.title: Rich source of energy
items.content: Rice provides complex carbohydrates that supply steady energy for growth and development.

items.title: Supports iron status
items.content: Fortification with iron helps prevent anemia, a common issue in young children.

items.title: Vitamin C for immunity
items.content: Vitamin C enhances iron absorption and supports the immune system.

items.title: Easy digestibility
items.content: Fine rice particles and lack of coarse fiber make the cereal gentle on a toddler’s digestive tract.

items.title: Allergen‑free
items.content: The product contains no nuts, dairy proteins or gluten, reducing the risk of allergic reactions.

items.title: Rice allergy
items.content: Although rare, some children may be allergic to rice. Discontinue use if any reaction occurs.

items.title: Iron excess
items.content: Frequent consumption of fortified cereal may lead to excess iron. Follow serving guidelines.

items.title: Not suitable for infants under 6 months
items.content: Babies younger than 6 months should receive breast milk or specialized formula.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mix 1 Tbsp of dry cereal with 150 ml of warm water or milk, stir, let stand for 2–3 minutes, then whisk to a smooth consistency. Add fruit puree if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the package in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. After opening, reseal tightly and use within 3 months.

content.title: About
content.content: Baby Toddler ham is a tender, cooked ham specially formulated for young children. It is made from selected pork meat, without artificial preservatives or colourings, and contains a low amount of salt to meet the nutritional needs of a growing body.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The ham is steam‑cooked, preserving most of its nutrients.
Only lean, skin‑free pork is used, reducing fat content.
The product meets strict infant‑food standards in the EU and the US.
Its soft texture is ideal for toddlers who are just learning to chew.
A single serving provides about 30 % of the daily iron requirement for 1‑3‑year‑olds.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Ham provides high‑quality animal protein essential for muscle and tissue growth.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: The iron in ham is highly bioavailable and helps prevent anemia in young children.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12 and niacin, supporting nervous system function and energy metabolism.

items.title: Low sodium
items.content: Limited salt content reduces strain on kidneys and the cardiovascular system.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Soft texture and lack of tough fibers make it gentle on a toddler’s digestive tract.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some children may be allergic to pork.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Although low, children with hypertension should monitor overall sodium intake.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Small pieces can pose a choking risk for children under 1 year; serve as puree or finely diced.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve Baby Toddler ham in small bite‑size pieces, stir into purees, cereals, or vegetable stews. Warm to room temperature before serving to keep it soft and palatable.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the ham refrigerated at 0 °C–4 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container. Once opened, use within 5 days. If frozen (‑18 °C or lower), it remains good for up to 3 months.

bread-reduced-calorie-and-or-high-fiber-.title: Bread, reduced calorie and/or high fiber, white or NFS, toasted

content.title: About
content.content: This is a white or whole‑grain bread made with reduced calories and/or increased dietary fiber. Toasted to a golden crust, it remains soft inside, offering a pleasant crunch on the outside.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Toasted bread has a slightly lower glycemic index than fresh bread due to partial starch breakdown.
Recipes often use sugar substitutes and whole grains to cut calories while boosting fiber content.
White bread can be fortified with B‑vitamins and iron, making it more nutritious.
Toasts are digested more easily in the morning, as heat accelerates starch gelatinization.
In some regions, NFS (non‑preservative formula) indicates bread made without artificial preservatives.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Increased dietary fiber supports healthy digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Reduced calorie content
items.content: Alternative ingredients lower the calorie count without sacrificing taste.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Complex carbohydrates provide steady energy over a longer period.

items.title: B‑vitamin complex
items.content: Fortified bread supplies thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin, essential for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It contains iron and magnesium, supporting blood formation and nerve function.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: People with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should avoid this product.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some versions may have higher salt levels; those with hypertension should check the label.

items.title: Oxidation
items.content: Toasted bread can lose freshness faster, so keep it in an airtight container.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy toasted slices as a snack, spread with low‑fat cottage cheese, avocado, or lean cheese, or use in sandwiches with turkey and vegetables. They pair well with sugar‑free fruit jams.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in a sealed bag. For longer storage keep in the refrigerator, and for a crisp crust freeze and re‑toast before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Part-skim mozzarella is a soft Italian cheese made from cow’s milk with reduced fat content (about 20 %). It has a mild buttery flavor, elastic texture, and characteristic “pearls” that melt and stretch when heated.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional mozzarella is made from water buffalo milk, but most commercial versions use cow’s milk.
The part-skim version retains most of the original taste while providing fewer calories.
Mozzarella is prized for its stretchability in pizza, lasagna, and baked dishes.
The cheese is often stored in brine, extending its shelf life for several weeks.
Italy celebrates a “Mozzarella Day” on September 13th.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Provides about 22 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus
items.content: Rich in calcium and phosphorus, which help strengthen bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12, riboflavin, and niacin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Reduced fat content
items.content: Compared with full‑fat mozzarella, it has less saturated fat, making it more suitable for lower‑fat diets.

items.title: Probiotic properties
items.content: Contains live cultures that may support a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Contains lactose, so individuals with intolerance should limit intake.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Some people may experience allergic reactions to casein.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Often stored in brine, which raises sodium levels; caution for those with hypertension.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Despite lower fat, it remains calorie‑dense at about 250 kcal per 100 g.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy fresh mozzarella in salads, melt it on pizza, stir it into pasta, or serve with fruit and nuts. Chill the cheese before slicing to help it hold its shape.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 1‑4 °C in its original brine or in an airtight container covered with plastic wrap. Once opened, use within 2‑3 weeks. Discard if it develops a sour odor or mold.

pizza-cheese-with-fruit-medium-crust.title: Cheese and Fruit Pizza, Medium Crust

content.title: About
content.content: Cheese and fruit pizza is an inventive twist on classic Italian pizza, pairing melted cheese with sweet fruit pieces such as pineapple, pear, or apple. The medium‑thick crust provides a crunchy edge and a soft interior, allowing the flavors to meld harmoniously.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The cheese‑and‑fruit combination became popular in the United States in the 1960s under the name “Hawaiian pizza.”
Traditional cheese for this pizza is mozzarella, but cheddar or gorgonzola are often used for a bolder taste.
Fruits balance the salty richness of the cheese and add a subtle acidity.
A medium crust is baked at 220‑250 °C for about 10‑12 minutes, yielding a golden surface while keeping the topping moist.
Some regions sprinkle walnuts or pecans on top for extra crunch.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Mozzarella and other cheeses provide a good amount of calcium, essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Vitamins from fruit
items.content: Fruits add vitamin C, vitamin A and antioxidants that support the immune system.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Cheese supplies complete protein needed for tissue repair and maintenance.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fruit and whole‑grain crust (if used) increase fiber content, aiding digestion.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Carbohydrates from the dough, fats from the cheese, and natural sugars from fruit give a quick and sustained energy supply.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cheese may cause discomfort for people who cannot digest lactose.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Many cheeses are salty, which can be an issue for those with hypertension.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to milk proteins.

items.title: Sugar in fruit
items.content: Sweet fruits raise the glycemic index of the dish, relevant for diabetics.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Cheese‑and‑fruit pizza is relatively high in calories, so portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pizza hot, cut into slices. Fresh basil or arugula can be added after baking for extra aroma. Optionally sprinkle nuts or drizzle a light barbecue sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to restore crust crispness.

summer-squash-yellow-or-green-frozen-coo.title: Summer squash, yellow or green, frozen, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Summer squash (yellow or green) are young fruits of the zucchini plant that are harvested, quickly blanched and flash‑frozen without any added fat. The freezing process retains a tender texture and mild flavor, and the vegetables can be cooked in a few minutes by steaming, microwaving or boiling.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Summer squash belongs to the Cucurbitaceae family and is closely related to zucchini and other gourds.
Yellow and green varieties differ only in skin colour; their nutritional profiles are virtually identical.
Freezing preserves most vitamins, especially vitamin C and beta‑carotene.
These squash are common in Asian cuisines, often added to soups and stir‑fries.
Because no fat is added, they are ideal for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Rich in vitamin A
items.content: Beta‑carotene, which converts to vitamin A, supports vision and immune function.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C acts as an antioxidant and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: One cup (≈150 g) of frozen summer squash provides about 30 kcal, making it excellent for weight management.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Provides potassium
items.content: Potassium supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Cucurbit allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to cucurbit vegetables.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Summer squash contains modest amounts of oxalates, which may be relevant for individuals prone to kidney stones.

items.title: Texture loss if overcooked
items.content: Overheating can make the squash watery and mushy.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook the squash by steaming or microwaving (2‑3 minutes), add to soups, stews, omelets, or use as a pizza topping. It also blends well into smoothies or can be pureed for baby foods.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen squash in a freezer at –18 °C or lower. Once thawed, use within 1‑2 days and do not refreeze.
